acidosis (BiCARB): a pragmatic randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003EP --- patients with CKD ,EGFR less than 30 not on hemodialysis\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI- sodium bicarbonate 3gm\/day for 2 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EC - placebo\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EO - Outcomes :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWe measured outcomes at baseline and 3, 6, 12 and 24\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Emonths. The primary outcome was the between-group\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Edifference in the Short Physical Performance Battery\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E(SPPB) at 12 months, adjusted for baseline values. The\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESPPB is a 12-point measure of lower limb strength and\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ebalance, with higher values denoting better function,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ethat predicts future disability, need for care and death. The minimum clinically important difference\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehas been derived for the measure [16].\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESecondary outcome measures were generic (EuroQoL\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEQ-5D-3L) [19] and disease-specific (Kidney Disease\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EQuality of Life) [20] health-related quality of life,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eanthropometry (weight, mid-arm muscle circumference, triceps\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eskinfold thickness, mid-thigh circumference), physical\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eperformance (6-min walk speed, grip strength) and renal\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Efunction\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgENeaEaFkGuEaR0MQZWE-0SthipMbde1UxTx05_Aarwwk2Yjhki6weHZfulagoC1zWfb5k0IfCZQAQp6e9c0sNjVNS2GM2cvK08tFeE-TfcSnoAzQTDNXn6m01OwIEQBwqhaLDxXwa6xQ\/s1600\/1654019019949109-4.png\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003EConclusion :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOur results suggest that at least for patients aged 60 and\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eover with CKD GFR categories 4 and 5, 1.5 to 3 g per day\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eof oral bicarbonate does not produce any health benefits\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eand may be associated with net harms. Whilst other indica-\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Etions for control of acidosis exist (for example high potas-\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Esium concentrations), evidence from the current trial\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Esuggests that the additional cost, treatment burden and side\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eeffects of oral bicarbonate may not justify its use in older\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Epeople with advanced CKD and mild degrees of metabolic\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eacidosis (i.e. serum bicarbonate concentration \u0026lt; 22 mmol\/\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EL). Raising bicarbonate levels by an amount sufficient to\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eproduce useful clinical effects will require larger doses than\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ewe used in this trial and is likely to require a ‘treat-to-target’\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Estrategy. However, such doses may not be tolerated by\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Emany older people. Alternative strategies, such as the use of\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehydrochloric acid binders, may provide a way round this\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eissue, but such agents need to be tested against current\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Epractice in representative groups of patients, using a range\r\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eof outcomes relevant to older people including
